newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to raise foreign stockholding further in '97.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to raise foreign stockholding further in '97.

text.p: South Korea plans to raise the foreign stock ownership limit to 25-26 percent this year from the current 23 percent, Yonhap Television News said on Monday.
It quoted a finance ministry report as saying the ceiling would be expanded further to 30 percent in 1998 and 35 percent in 1999 before complete liberalisation in 2000.
The ministry last week denied a similar newspaper report and said the limit would be raised to 26 percent in 1998 and 29 percent in 1999 before being scrapped in 2000.
Ministry officials were not available for comment on the Yonhap report during a public holiday.
The ceiling rose to 23 percent on May 2 from 20 percent.
Yonhap also said the ministry planned to allow foreigners this year to trade non-guaranteed convertible bonds issued by large companies.
Trading of such bonds would be allowed to foreigners in 1998, Yonhap said.
